questions.stem: According to the passage, what did Milutin Milankovitch propose about 100 years ago?
options: That cycles in Earth's orbit, tilt, and wobble affected Earth's long-term climate
That deep ocean temperatures cause ice ages
That human emissions would cause the next ice age
That ice ages occur randomly every 11,700 years
questions.evidence: The Serbian scientist Milutin Milankovitch developed a theory about 100 years ago that these cycles affected Earth’s long-term climate.
questions.explanation_ko: Milankovitch은 지구의 자전축 기울기, 흔들림, 궤도 모양의 주기가 장기 기후에 영향을 준다는 이론을 세웠다고 명시되어 있습니다.

questions.stem: According to the passage, all of the following were used by the research team EXCEPT:
options: Ice sheets across the northern half of the world
Deep ocean temperatures
Small regular changes in Earth's orbit over time
Direct measurements of current global emissions
questions.evidence: The scientists examined a million-year record of climate by looking at ice sheets across the northern half of the world and deep ocean temperatures.
questions.explanation_ko: 본문에는 얼음층, 해양 온도, 궤도 변화 자료는 언급되지만 현재 배출량 직접 측정은 언급되지 않습니다.

questions.stem: What can be inferred from Barker's statement about the difficulty of previous research?
options: Earlier scientists lacked the technology to measure Earth's orbit at all
Earlier research could not precisely link small orbital changes to large climate shifts
Milankovitch's theory was proven wrong by earlier studies
Ice ages have never been studied before this research
questions.evidence: He told the French News Agency (AFP) that for many years it has been difficult for scientists to show exactly how small changes in Earth’s orbit have led to huge changes between warm and cold periods.
questions.explanation_ko: 이전 연구자들이 작은 궤도 변화와 큰 기후 변화 사이의 정확한 연관성을 보여주기 어려웠다는 점에서, 이번 연구가 그 문제를 해결했다고 추론할 수 있습니다.

questions.stem: Why does the author mention that Barker's team studied slow changes over long periods instead of shorter periods?
options: To criticize Milankovitch's original theory
To explain how this study's method differed from and improved upon earlier research
To show that short-term climate change is more important than long-term change
To argue that human emissions are unrelated to climate cycles
questions.evidence: Barker said his team of researchers studied slow changes in temperature over long periods of time instead of only looking at shorter periods of change between cold and warm climates.
questions.explanation_ko: 이 문장은 이 연구팀이 기존 연구와 다른 방법(장기간의 느린 변화 연구)을 사용했다는 것을 설명하기 위해 언급되었습니다.

questions.stem: In the sentence "She said the study shows that changes in climate over tens of thousands of years are not random," what does the word "random" mean in this context?
options: Occurring without any predictable pattern or cause
Occurring very slowly
Occurring due to human activity
Occurring only in the northern hemisphere
questions.evidence: She said the study shows that changes in climate over tens of thousands of years are not random.
questions.explanation_ko: 'random'은 예측 불가능하고 특정한 원인 없이 일어나는 것을 의미하며, 여기서는 기후 변화가 예측 가능한 패턴을 따른다는 것을 강조합니다.

blanks.sentence_ko: 빙하기는 지구의 북부와 남부 넓은 지역을 얼음이 덮게 만드는 낮아진 기온의 시기이다.
세르비아 과학자 밀루틴 밀란코비치는 약 100년 전 이러한 주기가 지구의 장기적인 기후에 영향을 미친다는 이론을 개발했다.

blanks.meaning: 정확하게 시기를 특정하는 데 어려움을 겪다
blanks.sentence_ko: 그러나 연구자들은 각 기후 변화가 언제 일어났는지 정확하게 날짜를 특정하는 데 어려움을 겪었다.
그녀는 이 연구가 수만 년에 걸친 기후 변화가 무작위가 아니라는 것을 보여준다고 말했다.
그는 오랫동안 과학자들이 지구 궤도의 작은 변화가 어떻게 따뜻함과 추움 사이의 거대한 변화를 초래했는지 정확히 보여주기 어려웠다고 AFP에 말했다.

key_points: A new study suggests the next ice age will likely begin in about 11,000 years unless human emissions alter natural climate cycles.
Scientists studied three orbital factors: the shape of Earth's orbit, the tilt of its axis, and its wobble, based on Milankovitch's century-old theory.
The team examined a million-year climate record using ice sheets and deep ocean temperatures and compared it with orbital changes.
Unlike earlier research, this study focused on slow changes over long time periods rather than short-term shifts between warm and cold.
The research shows that long-term climate change follows predictable cycles rather than being random.
The team plans to further study how human activity might affect Earth's natural climate cycles.
main_idea: A new study using long-term climate and orbital data confirms that predictable cycles in Earth's orbit drive ice ages, suggesting the next one would begin in about 11,000 years absent human interference.
restate_sentence: The team noted that small changes in Earth’s orbit around the Sun caused predictable cycles of warming and cooling over a period of about 100,000 years.
